editorial:
Ever felt like you are the only one who doesn't have your life together? You will definitely feel that while watching this story about five college students struggling to find jobs. You get to follow Takuto, a quiet guy who spends more time watching people than talking. He is stuck in a weird spot because he has a crush on Mizuki, who used to date his upbeat roommate, Kotaro. Along with Rika, who is super driven, and Miyamoto, who hates the whole system but tries anyway, they all pretend to be okay on Twitter. It creates a really relatable vibe where you see the gap between the happy faces they show the world and the stress they feel inside.

What really works here is how the movie captures that awkward, scary transition into adulthood. The acting feels natural and not forced, making the quiet moments hit harder. While the pace is a bit slow at times, it fits the mood of being stuck in your own head. If you want the best experience, you should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for those crisp visuals. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great call. It is a perfect pick for anyone who feels lost in their twenties.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head as the students realize their social media personas were just masks. Takuto finally stops hiding his feelings and faces the truth about his relationships. Most of the group finds a path forward, though not in the way they expected. The movie ends on a hopeful note, showing that while the job search is stressful, they are not alone in their fear. They learn to be honest with themselves and each other.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic stories about growing up and finding a career.
